claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
When the load balancer's target group is passed in an ECS task definition's `portMappings`, AWSx uses that target group to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (`awsx.ecs` package) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw `aws.ecs` requires manual security group rule management.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The AWS provider has a LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
The ECS example program exports a stack output named `url` used by `pulumi stack output url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive than NLBs for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default, a load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
The load balancer accepts either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for an explicit list of subnets.
NLB listener `protocol` supports TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC; ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP and ALBs select HTTP or HTTPS based on port.
AWS docs page rule-action-types.html has fixed-response-actions and redirect-actions anchors.
AWS documentation page listener-rules.html covers listener rules.
`deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds and default is 300.
`slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable; disabled by default.
Target group `targetType` values are `instance`, `ip`, `lambda`, and `alb`; default is `instance`; IPs must be in VPC private range, RFC 1918, or RFC 6598 (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds, default 30 seconds.
`healthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3.
`unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3; for NLBs it must equal `healthyThreshold`.
Health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
